kind.definition: Having or showing a tender and considerate and helpful nature.
kind.exampleUsage: Salma was kind to the newcomer and listened to his questions.

generous.definition: Willing to give and share unstintingly.
generous.exampleUsage: Omar was generous and shared his supplies with the team.

honest.exampleUsage: Nadia was honest about the mistake she had made.
honest.definition: Telling the truth and behaving fairly without trying to deceive others.

brave.exampleUsage: Ali felt afraid but was brave enough to speak up.

patient.definition: Able to wait or handle difficulties without becoming upset.
patient.exampleUsage: The patient customer waited calmly during the delay.

loyal.exampleUsage: Her loyal friend supported her through a difficult period.

humble.exampleUsage: Despite winning the award, he remained humble about his success.

cheerful.definition: Being full of or promoting cheer.
cheerful.exampleUsage: The host gave the visitors a cheerful greeting.

reliable.exampleUsage: The reliable volunteer completed the work she had promised.

compassionate.exampleUsage: A compassionate colleague offered company to someone facing difficulty.

stubborn.exampleUsage: The fictional manager was stubborn and refused to reconsider the plan.
stubborn.definition: Unwilling to change your opinion or behavior despite other people's requests.

impatient.definition: Restless or short-tempered under delay or opposition.
impatient.exampleUsage: The guest grew impatient while waiting for the delayed bus.

shy.exampleUsage: She described herself as shy when meeting unfamiliar people.
shy.definition: Feeling nervous or uncomfortable around other people.

moody.exampleUsage: He said he felt moody after a tiring week.
moody.definition: Having moods that change noticeably or unpredictably.

selfish.definition: Concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others.
selfish.exampleUsage: The selfish character kept all the shared supplies for himself.

lazy.exampleUsage: In the story, the lazy character refused to make any effort.
lazy.definition: Unwilling to work or make an effort.

reckless.definition: Marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences.
reckless.exampleUsage: The reckless character ignored the warning about danger.

jealous.exampleUsage: The character felt jealous when her partner gave someone else more attention.
jealous.definition: Upset because someone has something or attention one wants.

arrogant.definition: Having or showing feelings of unwarranted importance out of overbearing pride.
arrogant.exampleUsage: The arrogant manager spoke as if nobody else’s ideas mattered.

pessimistic.exampleUsage: The pessimistic colleague expected the project to fail.

friendly.definition: Kind and welcoming toward other people.
friendly.exampleUsage: A friendly colleague welcomed the new team member.

outgoing.definition: Friendly and comfortable meeting and talking with other people.
outgoing.exampleUsage: He was outgoing and started conversations with unfamiliar guests.

introverted.definition: Preferring quieter situations and time alone or with a few close people.
introverted.exampleUsage: She described herself as introverted and preferred quieter company.

extroverted.exampleUsage: He described himself as extroverted and enjoyed busy social events.
extroverted.definition: Enjoying social situations and time with other people.

talkative.exampleUsage: The talkative guest spoke often during the meal.

quiet.definition: Usually speaking little in the social behavior sense taught here.
quiet.exampleUsage: The quiet participant spoke little but contributed an important idea.

charismatic.definition: Able to attract and influence others through personal appeal.
charismatic.exampleUsage: The charismatic facilitator held the group’s interest.

charming.exampleUsage: The host’s charming manner helped the guests feel welcome.
charming.definition: Pleasant and attractive in a way that makes people like you.

sociable.exampleUsage: The sociable neighbor enjoyed meeting new people.
sociable.definition: Enjoying meeting and spending time with other people.

reserved.exampleUsage: The reserved guest kept personal details private while joining the discussion.

hardworking.definition: Characterized by hard work and perseverance.
hardworking.exampleUsage: The hardworking volunteer kept making a steady effort.

creative.definition: Able to produce original ideas or make imaginative things.
creative.exampleUsage: The creative designer suggested an original use for the materials.

organized.definition: Good at planning tasks and keeping things in a clear order.
organized.exampleUsage: The organized team member kept the schedule and supplies in order.

ambitious.definition: Strongly wanting to achieve success or an important goal.
ambitious.exampleUsage: The ambitious learner hoped to lead a project one day.

punctual.definition: Acting or arriving or performed exactly at the time appointed.
punctual.exampleUsage: The punctual colleague arrived at the agreed time.

determined.definition: Firmly committed to achieving a goal despite difficulties.
determined.exampleUsage: She was determined to finish despite the setback.

dedicated.definition: Devoted to a cause or ideal or purpose.
dedicated.exampleUsage: The dedicated volunteer returned each week to support the project.

innovative.exampleUsage: The team’s innovative idea introduced a new method.
innovative.definition: Introducing new ideas, methods, or products.

focused.definition: Giving careful attention to one task or goal.
focused.exampleUsage: He stayed focused while completing the difficult step.

resourceful.exampleUsage: The resourceful organizer found a solution using the available materials.
resourceful.definition: Good at finding practical ways to solve problems.

sensitive.definition: Easily affected by feelings or aware of other people's emotions.
sensitive.exampleUsage: She was sensitive to her colleague’s feelings and chose her words carefully.

empathetic.definition: Showing empathy or ready comprehension of others' states.
empathetic.exampleUsage: The empathetic friend tried to understand the speaker’s experience.

calm.definition: Not feeling or showing strong agitation, fear, or anger.
calm.exampleUsage: The calm facilitator helped organize the discussion during the delay.

anxious.exampleUsage: Ali said he felt anxious about the presentation’s outcome.
anxious.definition: Feeling worried or nervous about what might happen.

optimistic.definition: Hopeful that things will go well.
optimistic.exampleUsage: The optimistic team member expected a good outcome.

confident.definition: Feeling sure of your abilities or decisions.
confident.exampleUsage: After preparing, Leila felt confident about her presentation.

insecure.exampleUsage: He felt insecure about the unfamiliar task and asked for guidance.
insecure.definition: Not feeling confident or safe about oneself or a situation.

passionate.definition: Showing strong interest or enthusiasm for something.
passionate.exampleUsage: She was passionate about learning and spoke with strong enthusiasm.

thoughtful.definition: Showing care for other people's needs and feelings.
thoughtful.exampleUsage: The thoughtful organizer considered everyone’s needs.

dramatic.definition: Showing strong emotions or reactions that may seem exaggerated.
dramatic.exampleUsage: In the story, the dramatic character reacted with exaggerated surprise.
